storedTranscript.text: Hello, I'm Ryota, and welcome to your English lesson! Today we'll talk about your work and a project you've been involved in, and practise two grammar points: the present perfect and the past simple. Does that sound good to you?
Yes.

Great, let's begin. You'll talk about your job and a project you're proud of, practise the present perfect and the past simple, and try follow-up questions. I'll correct your mistakes, explain them, and give you a chance to try again. If you'd like, we can also practise pronunciation at the end. First there's a short, friendly level check so I can adjust the lesson for you. Are you ready?
Yes.

Wonderful. Let's start with a short conversation so I can see what you can already do. Please answer in English, and don't worry about mistakes.

Can you tell me a little about your job? What do you do?
I, I work as admin at the company.
Thanks, that's clear. What kind of admin work do you do?
I do accounting and some admin work.
Accounting is a useful area to know well. Have you ever worked with an international customer? If so, can you tell me about the experience?
No.
No problem.
No, I didn't.
That's fine. Can you tell me about a difficult task or project you worked on at your company?
What do you mean by important project?

Good question. I mean any work task or project that took time or effort, for example a big report, a new system, or an event your team organized. It can be small or big. Can you tell me about one task you did at work?
The year end tax. system comparison.

Thanks. A year-end tax system comparison is a good example of real work. Now let's look at two tenses you can use when you talk about your job.

Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Yes.

Let's move on to talking about your work. 仕事について話すときは、短い文を使うと分かりやすいです。

ここにある文を、ひとつずつ読んでみてください。Now, what do you do at work? Please answer with one or two short sentences.
I'm checking emails and sorting out some paperwork.

その文は正しいです。メールの確認と書類の整理ですね。

では、今の仕事の文をもうひとつ言ってみましょう。Try starting with: "I work in..."

Does that make sense?
Yes.
わかりました。では、今の仕事について、あなたの言葉で一文言ってみてください。Try starting with: "I work in..."
I do emails and sorting out some documents.

いいですね、仕事の内容がよく分かります。「I do emails」は少し不自然なので、「I handle emails」と言うのが自然です。

Now you say it, please: "I handle emails and documents."
Please, could you please rephrase that, please?

わかりました。別の言い方にします。「I take care of emails and documents.」は「メールと書類を担当しています」という意味です。

Now you say it, please: "I take care of emails and documents."
Yes.

仕事の練習はここまでです。次は現在完了を練習しましょう。まず、お手本を言います。 "I take care of emails and documents."

現在完了は have か has と過去分詞を使い、今も続いている期間や経験を話すときに使います。

では、質問です。どのくらい今の会社で働いていますか。Try starting with: "I have worked..."

How long have you worked at your current company? Answer with a full sentence, starting with "I have worked".
I have worked for the current company for ten years.

すばらしいです。「I have worked ... for ten years」は現在完了で正しく言えています。ひとつだけ直すと、「for the current company」は「at my current company」と言うほうが自然です。

次は過去形です。特定の時期に終わった出来事には、過去形を使います。

Next is past simple. Shall we go on, or do you have a question first?
Yes.

では、過去形を練習しましょう。過去形は、特定の時に終わった出来事に使います。

では質問です。あなたはいつ今の会社に入りましたか。Try starting with: "I joined my company in..."

When did you join your company? Answer with a full sentence, starting with "I joined my company in".
I don't really know.
That's okay. Let's make it easier: you don't need the exact date. You can just say the year, like "2015", or "about ten years ago". Try starting with: "I joined my company in..."
Two.

「Two」だけでは、いつ入社したのか分かりません。年を言ってもらえますか。たとえば「I joined my company in 2015.」のように、Try starting with: "I joined my company in..."

Does that make sense?
Could you explain that in Japanese?

はい、日本語で説明します。

英語で「I joined my company in 2015.」と言うと、「私は2015年に会社に入りました」という意味です。「join」は「入る」という意味で、過去の終わったできごとなので、過去形の「joined」を使います。年を言うだけで大丈夫ですよ。

では、もう一度言ってみてください。Try starting with: "I joined my company in..."
I have worked for my current company for 10 years.

現在完了の形は正しいです。ただ、前に直した「at」がまだ残っています。「for my current company」ではなく「at my current company」と言います。

では、過去形の質問にもう一度答えてください。あなたはいつ今の会社に入りましたか。Try starting with: "I joined my company in..."

Are you with me so far?
I want uh improve my speaking skill because I often attend a meeting.
that use English.

Of course, I'll use English. Here is the sentence: "I joined my company in 2015."

Now let's try the past simple with your work. Did you do the year-end tax system comparison alone, or with a team?
Uh, what do you mean?
Sorry, that was unclear. When you did the year-end tax system comparison, did you work alone, or with other people?
No, I don't really did work closely with her on the project.
Not quite. After "didn't," we use the basic verb, so it's "didn't work," not "didn't did work." Try the whole sentence again, starting with: "I didn't..."
No, I didn't really work closely with her on the project.
Yes, that's right: "I didn't really work closely with her on the project." Now let's use the past simple for the tax comparison. When did you finish it? Try starting with: "I finished it in..."
I finished accounting yesterday.

Yes, that's right: "I finished accounting yesterday." You used the past simple for a finished task at a specific time. Now, what did you do at work last month? Try starting with: "I finished..." or "I worked on..."
because we implemented a new system for tax system this year and I was successfully finished all the new taxes on time.

Good, you explained the reason clearly. One thing to fix: "I was successfully finished" is not quite right here. Use the past simple verb directly: "I successfully finished..." Try the whole sentence again, starting with: "I successfully finished..."
I successfully finished the new tasks because we implemented a new task system this year.

Yes, that's right: "I successfully finished the new tasks because we implemented a new task system this year." Your past simple is clear and accurate.

That's the past simple done. Next is a longer conversation about your work. What is one project you are proud of?
that I think successfully finished the new tasks because we implement a new system for tax.
year in tax system.
The year-end tax system project, I see. Can you make it a full sentence? Try starting with: "I worked on..."
that that everything was new, that we didn't know them we we didn't have a manual to follow on.

Everything being new is a clear reason, and "we didn't have" is correct past simple. One small thing: we say "a manual to follow," without "on." Can you say the whole sentence again, starting with "We didn't have a manual..."?
Could you repeat that, please?
Of course. The small point was this: we say "a manual to follow," without "on." Can you say the whole sentence again, starting with "We didn't have a manual..."?
I don't really remember, but maybe helps from our accounting office staff.

That's fine, asking your colleagues is a good idea. Here is the sentence: "We didn't have a manual to follow."

Now, how did your team finish everything on time without a manual? Try starting with: "We..."
Uh, she's from the or accounting office admin.
So she's from the accounting office admin team, and she helped you with the project. Thanks for explaining. What did she help you with? Try starting with: "She helped me..."
I cannot share the name.
No problem, you don't need to say her name. Just tell me what she helped you with. Try starting with: "She helped me..."
new.
Did you mean she helped you with the new system? Please say the full sentence, starting with "She helped me with..."
Could you repeat that, please?

Of course. She helped you with the new system, so you can say: "She helped me with the new system." Please say that sentence.

Are you with me so far?
Yes.

Here it is, from me: "She helped me with the new system."

That finishes our talk about your project. Next is an optional pronunciation practice on a few words from today. Would you like to do it, or shall we go straight to the summary?
How to communicate with the non in not the Japanese people with not the with people with the in and not from Japan.

Did you ask how to communicate with people who are not from Japan? (日本語で確認です。日本以外の人と、どうやって話すかという質問ですか。)

If so, one useful sentence is: "I communicate with customers by email."

Is that the question you meant?
Yes.

Yes, email is a good way to reach people outside Japan.

Today you talked about your work and a project you were proud of. Your present perfect was accurate: "I have worked at my current company for ten years." Your past simple was clear in your project story. To improve, say "finished" rather than "was finished," and "follow" without "on." Pronunciation can wait for next time.

Well done today. Keep using these two grammar points when you talk about your work. Thank you, and see you next time!
